title: Row-major strides
hints: In a row-major buffer the last axis moves fastest, so its stride is 1.
One step along axis `d` skips over a whole block made of every axis after `d`.
Multiply `shape[d+1]`, `shape[d+2]`, ... up to the last axis. For the last axis that product is empty, which is 1.

answer.explain: The stride of axis `d` is the product of the sizes of all later axes, starting from 1. The loop runs from `d + 1` to `ndim - 1`, so the last axis correctly gets the empty product, 1.
